reason: Cline preparation blocked: Issue #255 'Add Nitrokey Pro and PKCS#11 support' is a maintainer-labeled EPIC (label: EPIC) feature request, not a concrete repository change, and its funding is withdrawn. Withdrawn funding: the admission's claim is a $200 USD Bountysource bounty recorded at https://github.com/keepassxreboot/keepassxc/issues/255#issuecomment-569517148 ('Added $200 bounty, get to work guys!', droidmonkey, 2019-12-29). The same payer/project lead later removed it: 'We don't endorse any bounty system anymore' (droidmonkey, 2023-01-30, issuecomment-1425171200) and, answering a direct 'is the bounty still available?' question on 2025-10-03, 'Also, there are no bounties.' (droidmonkey, 2025-10-04, issuecomment-3366106387). The Bountysource platform is also dead: https://app.bountysource.com/issues/41676090-add-nitrokey-pro-and-pkcs-11-support and https://api.bountysource.com/issues/41676090 both fail to resolve (curl exit 6 / HTTP 000). No live, verifiable funding remains. Generic product idea without an agreed repository change: the issue is an open-ended architecture request spanning 2017-02-04 to 2026-04-01 with 155 comments and 140 reactions and no agreed design; the maintainer explicitly discourages it: 'Doing PKCS#11 with the current KDBX spec creates a huge mess. I DO NOT recommend working on this at all.' (droidmonkey, 2025-10-04, issuecomment-3366106387). The design is still contested as of 2026-04-01 (CardContact vs droidmonkey vs phoerious on on-device AES vs derived-key wrapping), and maintainer phoerious states any PKCS#11 PR 'should be integrated with the ongoing work on FIDO2 (which should be merged first I think)' (2026-03-31, issuecomment-4162875175), pointing at the still-open, unmerged groundwork PR #10311. This requires a full redesign of KDBX key derivation (phoerious, 2026-04-01: 'this would require a full redesign of how we encrypt and decrypt files'), not a focused code-level fix. No competing implementation PR exists yet (GitHub search: repo:keepassxreboot/keepassxc 'pkcs11' in:title type:pr => 0; 'nitrokey' type:pr => 2, both closed challenge-response PRs #9397/#9631), so the sole disqualifier is withdrawn funding plus the absence of a bounded, maintainer-sanctioned code change. Per the classification rule, a withdrawn-funding and generic-product-epic issue must be written as blocked, so the checkout was left unchanged (no worktree was created at /tmp/bounty-workspaces/repos/keepassxreboot--keepassxc--255).
